key_insight: A simple nonconvex pipeline—link-aware initialization, rowwise refinement, and plain gradient descent—can yield provably accurate inference for generalized latent factor models with missing data, even without explicit debiasing or incoherence constraints.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a practical way to estimate latent structure and quantify uncertainty in sparse, non-Gaussian high-dimensional data such as recommender systems, sensor arrays, and LLM capability evaluation.
method: Link-aware double-SVD initialization tailored to the exponential-family link
Unilateral refinement to obtain rowwise consistency and a contraction-friendly region
Vanilla gradient descent with implicit regularization to reach statistical error
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulations and an application to large language model evaluation, where the method supports uncertainty-aware estimation and ranking of latent capabilities.
watch_item: Performance and inference guarantees depend on reaching the refined initialization region; in practice, severe missingness or weak signal may make this stage sensitive to tuning and model mismatch.
paper_title: From Good Starts to Optimal Inference: Generalized Latent Factor Models with Missingness and Implicit Regularization
